content.title: Micro-Contact Activates Megastructure | Glyph Trigger, Concentric Expansion, Portal Reveal
content.summary: A contour disk expands into a suspended terrain sphere after one traced notch. Preserve the five causal invariants and terminal proof while replacing every source-specific surface.

quick_start.input_format: One bounded object establishes the inactive baseline. + One visible contact is the sole trigger. + Activation propagates outward in readable order. + The adult and origin marker preserve scale and geography. + The terminal frame holds origin, transformed environment and reaction.
quick_start.recommended_input: Place one adult cave cartographer before a palm-sized brass contour disk in a stone archive. Carry the line through three concentric floor rings, activating them from near to far. Hold the adult reaction and the complete glowing sphere with the original disk still visible below.
required_anchors: One bounded object establishes the inactive baseline.
One visible contact is the sole trigger.
The adult and origin marker preserve scale and geography.
The terminal frame holds origin, transformed environment and reaction.
usage_steps: Replace the example subject, setting, and surface details with an original concept.
Keep every required anchor and Creative DNA invariant causally visible.
Choose the MiniMax H3 or Seedance 2.0 prompt and fill only the declared variable slots.
Check duration, event order, camera continuity, sound, and anti-copy constraints before generation.
applicable_scope: A contour disk expands into a suspended terrain sphere after one traced notch. Preserve the five causal invariants and terminal proof while replacing every source-specific surface.
Original 4–15 second concepts that can preserve every required anchor.
MiniMax H3 or Seedance 2.0 projects that need a reusable causal video structure.
not_suitable_for: Requests that copy the source identity, setting, props, dialogue, or shot order.
Concepts that cannot show all required anchors inside the target duration.
Long-form exposition or unrelated multi-location stories without a compact causal chain.
